resources.string: The app can\'t install packages on this router
That needs the LuCI Software page (luci-app-package-manager, or luci-app-opkg before 24.10). Anything already installed still shows up and can be set up here.
It\'s installed, but its LuCI part (%1$s) is missing, and that\'s what lets the app configure it.
It\'s installed, but the router hasn\'t loaded it yet. The network needs a restart: a few seconds without connection.
The router will download %1$s and whatever it needs from the OpenWrt servers. It needs internet.
When it finishes, the network restarts: a few seconds without internet at home.
A firmware update removes installed packages; the app will let you know and you can install it again.
This phone will no longer be able to reach the router from outside home. It keeps working at home. You have to do this from home: the app removes it over the direct connection.
%1$s will no longer be able to reach the router from outside home.
Checks whether the router can be reached from the internet: the app tries over your mobile data, without leaving Wi-Fi. Uses a few KB.
The router can be reached from outside.
Can\'t check with this mobile data.
The router can\'t be reached from outside.
Only the app uses the tunnel, with its own WireGuard: it doesn\'t take the phone\'s VPN or touch others. Through the tunnel you can only reach the router\'s web page, not the rest of the network.
The router has no public address right now (neither IPv6 nor IPv4 without CGNAT): it can\'t be reached from outside.
It\'s reached over IPv6 (%1$s): the network you connect from must have IPv6 too.
WireGuard on UDP port %1$d · not up
From outside, the app will look for it at %1$s.
Without dynamic DNS, the app will use the last address it saw: if it changes while you\'re away, it won\'t find the router.

resources.string: Remote access needs it: without a fixed name, if your provider changes the router\'s address while you\'re away, the app won\'t find it.
For remote access: a name that always points to the router.
The router has no public IPv6 to publish right now.
Username (if the URL asks for one)
The router\'s IPv4 and IPv6 will be published: that way it can be reached from any network.
The router\'s IPv4 will be published.
The router\'s IPv6 will be published: with CGNAT, IPv4 can\'t be used to get in from outside.
This queue is on %1$s, but the internet connection is %2$s: this way it does nothing. Edit it to change it.
Write the speed without thousands separators (e.g. 1000).
Run a speed test with nobody else using the internet and enter a bit less (85–95 %): if you enter more than the connection gives, it won\'t help at all.
It\'s on, but the service isn\'t running.
No device can open ports on its own.
The router\'s internet address (%1$s) is private: there\'s another router in front or your provider uses CGNAT. So UPnP can\'t open ports to the internet over IPv4.
Each device can only open ports to itself. Best left on.
